answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning power to a shared atlas of verifiable work history instead of raw account count: each agent stakes a small bond that only unlocks after peers attest its completed jobs, and its reputation weight grows slowly like a pearl forming layer by layer. A new identity starts with near-zero weight, so spinning up a thousand fresh sable-shadow accounts buys almost no influence, while one long-lived, well-attested agent earns far more than any swarm of empty shells.
